title: We ran out of IP addresses

yt.title: The internet ran out of addresses. Here is the math #Shorts
yt.description:
IPv4 uses 32 bits: 2^32 addresses. World population from the World Bank (SP.POP.TOTL, {people_year}). Numbers are computed by code.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.text: The internet ran out of addresses
scenes.narration: The internet ran out of addresses. Here is the math.
An IPv4 address has thirty two bits. That gives only {ipv4_say} billion addresses. The world has about {people_say} billion people.

scenes.label: bits in an IPv6 address
scenes.narration: IPv6 fixes this with one hundred twenty eight bits. That is more addresses than grains of sand on Earth.

scenes.text: Your home shares one public IP
scenes.narration: Until everyone switches, your router shares one public address between all your devices. That trick is called NAT.
